taxonomy.note: Kew/POWO accepts Vernonia baldwinii and also recognizes two varieties. The Texas infraspecific treatment is Vernonia baldwinii var. interior; the project source concept remains at accepted species rank for the learner/review queue.

sources.label: Kew POWO — Vernonia baldwinii var. interior

evidence.detail: UT Austin Plant Resources Center Travis County Asteraceae herbarium index lists both Vernonia baldwinii and Vernonia lindheimeri.
UT Austin Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County search includes both Vernonia baldwinii and Vernonia lindheimeri.
Harvard GH specimen 01925576, A. A. Heller 1927, collected about Kerrville, Kerr County, determined Vernonia baldwinii.

morphology.learner_core: Tall robust ironweed with broader rough leaves and broad terminal clusters of purple discoid heads; no rays.
morphology.refinement: Texas plants belong to the broad-leaved western ironweed concept; leaves are much broader than in V. lindheimeri. Current FNA/WFO descriptions emphasize ovate to lance-ovate blades with hairy/tomentose undersides and flattened to irregular terminal arrays.
morphology.comparison: V. lindheimeri has very narrow linear leaves, densely woolly beneath, usually glabrate above, and strongly revolute margins. V. × guadalupensis may be intermediate; do not force intermediate flowering plants to a parent.
